s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin lesions with hyperkeratotic plaques
salient_findings: Pruritic lesions on the scrotum and buttock
Annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with atrophic center and elevated edge
Hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, and parakeratotic columns on histopathology
key_facts: 10-year history of pruritic lesions
Lesions located on scrotum, buttock, groin, and intergluteal cleft
Previous treatment at local clinic with little improvement
No relevant medical history
No family history of similar skin problems
Normal or negative routine blood work, syphilis serologies, and HIV testing
Histopathological examination revealed hyperkeratosis and parakeratotic columns
Perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
No inguinal adenopathy

shortlist.label: Darier's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and dyskeratotic keratinocytes are characteristic of Darier's disease

shortlist.label: Grover's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Pruritic lesions and hyperkeratotic plaques are consistent with Grover's disease

shortlist.label: Porokeratosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of parakeratotic columns and hyperkeratosis suggests porokeratosis

shortlist.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pruritic lesions and hyperkeratotic plaques are seen in lichen simplex chronicus

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperkeratotic plaques and perivascular infiltration of lymphocytes can be seen in psoriasis

raw.rationale: The presence of hyperkeratosis, irregular papillomatosis, parakeratotic columns (cornoid lamella), and dyskeratotic keratinocytes in the histopathological examination are characteristic features of porokeratosis, which matches the clinical presentation of annular gray hyperkeratotic plaques with an atrophic center and a slightly elevated edge.

rejected.label: Darier's disease
rejected.why: Darier's disease typically presents with greasy, crusted papules in seborrheic areas and suprabasal acantholysis on histology, which does not match the provided case facts.

rejected.label: Grover's disease
rejected.why: Grover's disease is characterized by sudden onset of pruritic papules, often with a distinctive 'nutmeg grater' appearance on the skin, which does not align with the 10-year history and specific lesion characteristics in this case.

rejected.label: Lichen simplex chronicus
rejected.why: Lichen simplex chronicus typically presents with thickened, hyperpigmented plaques due to chronic scratching, which does not match the specific histopathological findings of parakeratotic columns and cornoid lamellae in this case.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: Psoriasis is characterized by well-defined erythematous plaques with silvery scales, and histologically by regular epidermal hyperplasia and parakeratosis without the specific features of cornoid lamellae seen in porokeratosis.
